claim: An in-toto MATCH rule in a signed layout constrains the step it names, so a rule whose destination step does not exist still checks something.

environment.what: in-toto artifact rules as implemented in the python package
assumptions: layout with a single step and one link

counterexample.means: a layout whose only rule points at a step that does not exist verifies successfully — the rule consumes nothing and forbids nothing

negative_control.means: the same layout with a terminal DISALLOW * is refused, so the protection comes from closing the rule set, not from the MATCH

applies_until: in-toto reports a rule whose destination step is absent from the layout, or the rule language stops treating consumption and existence as separate questions.

cost.to_discover: an afternoon, most of it spent building a layout that verifies at all
cost.to_recheck: seconds, in a venv holding in-toto 3.1.0
